To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the high diversity of antioxidant defenses in animals is the result of the evolution of structural, biochemical, and physiological mechanisms to cope with the deleterious effects of reactive species, and that the study of these mechanisms can be used to understand the evolution of life history and maternal/epi-genetic inheritance.

the study of antioxidant mechanisms has the potential to identify the costs of oxidative stress, to quantify the contribution of maternal/epigenetics to the phenotype, and to identify the link between life-history traits and antioxidant mechanisms.

animals have evolved a high diversity of molecular and structural antioxidant defense mechanisms, that these defense mechanisms are evolutionary conserved, and that they can have a high energetic cost, thus affecting trade-offs between different life-history strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how antioxidant responses are integrated in the whole animal, how they affect life-history trade-offs, and how they are transmitted from parents to offspring.
the biochemical integration of antioxidant systems and the link between life-history trade-offs, epigenetic inheritance, and maximum life span.
the evolution of antioxidant defenses in animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single antioxidant response to stress, and that the study of the biochemical integration of different redox systems will be a major challenge for the future.
there is a high degree of diversity and conservation in antioxidant defenses, and this knowledge could be used to evaluate the potential costs and benefits of these mechanisms.
the evolution of antioxidant mechanisms has been shaped by a complex interaction among the environment, life-history strategies, maternal effects, and epigenetic mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the biochemical integration of different redox systems, which is the result of a complex interplay between structural and molecular antioxidant defenses, is the key to understanding the evolution of oxidative stress resistance and the link with life span.
the study of antioxidant responses to reactive oxygen species is an important area for research on evolutionary ecology.
the biochemical integration of different redox systems and antioxidant defenses is essential to understanding how organisms deal with reactive species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better understanding of the mechanisms of the redox system in animals can be used to understand the mechanisms of aging and longevity, and to develop new strategies to improve human health.
the study of the biochemical integration of the different redox systems is essential to understand the mechanisms of antioxidant response and its evolutionary and ecological significance.
the study of molecular mechanisms of antioxidant defenses in animals is a promising field that will help understand how the organism integrates the redox state with its physiology.
